//: The first years (docs/ACADEMY.md, "The first years"): the steps pinned at the top of the list on the right in a first game, written for each start, and what the Academy's lectures fold to. A step's "done" says what ticks it: "report" (a report answered), "did:<act>" (vote, fleet, buy, venture, build, law: an act the player did by their own hand), "seen:<window>" or "seen:<window>:<tab>" (a window or tab opened), "seen:map" (a world picked on the map); alternatives are joined by |. "show" is where Show me goes (a window id with its tab after a colon, "office", "galaxy" for the map, "fleet" for the house's first fleet). "ring" names what Show me lights (the client's FirstYears.razor knows them). "term" is the Academy's term the step carries onto the real screen. "needs" keeps a step only for a house that has the thing (world, fleet) or, with !, lacks it.
terms: the House ledger and the Exchange

notYet.vote: Nothing is before the Senate this year. What the houses move now is voted next year.

the_old_lion.title: Answer a report
the_old_lion.text: Reports wait in the list on the right and in your Office. Open one, read what each answer costs and gives, and choose.

the_old_lion.title: Order your fleet
the_old_lion.text: Pick The Lion's Fleet in the list on the right, click a world on the map, then press Send. Nothing is ordered until you do.

the_old_lion.title: Read the House ledger

the_old_lion.title: Declare your vote

the_senate.summary: The houses govern the Reach through the Senate, and each votes by its weight: its influence in the chamber, its rank and any office it holds. A motion waits a year on the docket while the houses are lobbied, and is voted at the end of the next. Four parties sit in the chamber, and every tenth year they elect two consuls, each with a veto.
the_senate.imperium: One house holds the throne, and with it every office of the Reach: there are no consuls and no elections. The Senate still sits and votes by weight, and a motion still waits a year on the docket before it is voted. The parties remain as habits of voting, and the Emperor's own edict sets the throne's temper toward the houses.

houses_and_rank.summary: A house climbs a ladder of rank that outlives everyone in it, from Citizen to First Citizen; a person climbs a career in one of three services, which starts again with every generation. Legitimacy says how much rank a house can carry, and holding more than it supports breeds trouble every year. Rise too fast and the other houses join against you.
houses_and_rank.imperium: A house climbs a ladder of noble titles, from Knight to Archduke and the throne; a person climbs a career in one of three services, which starts again with every generation. Legitimacy says how much title a house can carry, and holding more than it supports breeds trouble every year. Rise too fast and the houses, then the throne itself, take notice.

estates_and_law.summary: Six estates, from the Commons to the Frontier, judge your house by the laws it sets, on a scale from 0 to 100. A loyal estate pays you; a hostile one costs you and stirs up your worlds. Changing a law costs influence, and an estate hostile across the Reach takes its case to the Senate.

coin.summary: A house lives on credits, materials, manpower and influence, from the worlds it holds and the ventures it owns. Helium-3 fuels the fleet, rare earths build the heavy hulls and isotopes arm them, and not every world has them. The House window's ledger shows every line of what comes in and goes out.

fleets.summary: A fleet's power is its hulls, weighed by their class, readiness, the admiral, veterancy and your orders: its stance, where you command from, its supply and its crews' loyalty. The line beats the press, the press beats the skirmish, and the skirmish beats the line. Fleets cross the map a lane a year; everything else about them is in the Military window.

beyond_the_reach.summary: The Reach is three rings: a rich and loyal core, a middle that leans either way, and a poor, lawless rim where raiders gather and worlds break away. Five nations lie beyond the rim, and the Senate makes war on them by vote. A house may send a fleet abroad for plunder, and a general who wins abroad comes home with a name.

the_turn.summary: Once you pass out, a turn is a year: reports come to your Office, you answer what you can afford, act in any window, and end the year. Influence, treasury actions and agents refill a little each year and hold 6 at most. The list on the right shows what waits for you.

the_exchange.summary: Everything a house makes or burns has a price on the Exchange, and war and scarcity move it. A venture is a business the house owns, worth about 6 years of what it earns, and it can be listed as a company of 100 shares. Whoever holds more than half the shares directs the company.

the_dynasty.summary: You are one life in a house that outlives you: when you die you play your heir, who keeps what the house holds and starts a career from the first rung. Marriage brings allies, claims and children, and kin with ambition and no prospects are a danger. The cadets of your year are the heads you will sit beside in the Senate for the rest of your life.

tips.banner: A Standard that loses its banner costs each of its cadets 2 standing. Answers that win your Standard strength keep its banner up.
tips.marks: Read what you already know: a subject gives 3 marks and 1 more for each point of its skill you have, up to 3 more. {subject} would give you {marks}.
tips.standing: Standing counts twice in the order of merit. Bold answers before the instructors raise it; careless ones lower it.
tips.first: Hold the lead: the other cadets gained {low} to {high} marks each this term, so a lead melts unless your standing keeps rising.
tips.rising: You are climbing. Keep earning standing: each point of it is worth 2 marks, and the other cadets gain {low} to {high} a term.
tips.pace: The other cadets gained {low} to {high} marks each this term. To climb past them, earn standing: each point of it is worth 2 marks.
tips.last: The top third of the year pass out with honours, and the first of the year lifts the house's legitimacy by 3.
